زَائِرٌ , applied to a lion, Roaring, or growling; i. e. making his cry, or voice, to be heard (S, A, K) in his chest, (S, A,) or from his chest; (K;) as also ↓ زَئِرٌ , (S, K, TA,) like كَتِفٌ, (TA,) [in the CK, erroneously, زَئِيرٌ,] and ↓ مُزْئِرٌ . (K.) ―
-b2- Also (assumed tropical:) An enemy: (TA:) the pl. زَائِرُونَ is thus used by 'Antarah. (S, TA.) ―
-b3- And (assumed tropical:) Angry: (IAar, TA:) and so زَيِرٌ; but original with hemzeh: so says AM. (TA. [See also زَئِرٌ.])
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
